title: History and Evolution of Kotlin
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of history and evolution of kotlin using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates history and evolution of kotlin.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **History and Evolution of Kotlin** as part of **Introduction to Kotlin**. Language versions, compiler versions, plugins, and library versions evolve independently enough that release notes and compatibility tables must be checked. Use the subtopics—Kotlin's Origins and Development, Major Language Milestones, Kotlin's Release and Compatibility Model—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Clear fundamentals help you reason about program behavior before adding abstraction. Small input/output checks make syntax and control flow easier to debug.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Language versions, compiler versions, plugins, and library versions evolve independently enough that release notes and compatibility tables must be checked.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with kotlin's origins and development. Then compare it with major language milestones. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: Kotlin's Origins and Development
items.text: Kotlin's Origins and Development is one part of history and evolution of kotlin. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

items.title: Kotlin's Release and Compatibility Model
items.text: Kotlin's Release and Compatibility Model means checking the boundary between the language feature and its compiler, runtime, plugin, library, or target version. Pin the versions used by the project and verify documented support before depending on the behavior.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Save the snippet in a Kotlin/JVM console project and run the configured Gradle application task, or use the Kotlin Playground for examples that need no external dependencies.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: History and Evolution of Kotlin removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.

items.title: Explain
items.text: Describe the main rule of history and evolution of kotlin in your own words.

items.title: Apply
items.text: Change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

items.title: Verify
items.text: Check one edge case and the official reference for the selected Kotlin/runtime version.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small variation that demonstrates history and evolution of kotlin. Write down your predicted result first, run it in the correct local project, then explain one boundary case involving kotlin's origins and development.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain history and evolution of kotlin without copying the lesson wording.
Demonstrate the concept with a small code/configuration change and state the expected result.
Test one boundary case or explain a relevant platform/version limitation.
hints: Begin with the first syllabus subtopic: Kotlin's Origins and Development. What input or state does it act on?
